baslik: The Physics That Makes Explosions Deadly
hook: Its not the fire that kills
aciklama:
An explosion kills in a way most people misunderstand. It is not the flames - it is a wall of pressure moving faster than sound.

#shorts #physics #science #engineering #explosion

sahneler.metin: An explosion does not kill mainly with fire.
It kills with a wall of air moving faster than sound.
In an instant, solid material becomes rapidly expanding gas.
That gas slams outward as a shockwave, crushing what is near.
The overpressure can burst lungs and eardrums before the heat arrives.
Then air rushes back to fill the gap.
That reverse pull drags debris back toward the blast.
Distance is everything, because the pressure drops fast as it spreads.

vaka.ders: blast engineers design with distance first
vaka.yanilgi: The fireball is the scary part on camera, but overpressure — the shockwave — does most of the damage.
vaka.tartisma: Blast engineers say distance beats walls. Would you trust a blast wall, or distance?
